title: Context Engineering for Healthcare AI Agents
body:
Diagnosing and tuning agent behavior from MLflow traces
Hands-on workshop • Tony Farias • 2026

title: Context engineering is becoming a discipline—not just a technique.
body: The shift: from polishing one prompt to governing everything an agent can see, use, and remember.

title: The market signal: organizations are naming the role
body:
1,000 CONTEXT ENGINEERS

Cognizant announced plans to deploy 1,000 Context Engineers with Workfabric AI, supported by its ContextFabric platform, to industrialize enterprise agentic AI.

Why it matters: context quality, governance, and domain knowledge are moving from implicit craft to explicit operating capability.

Source: Cognizant, Aug. 29, 2025

title: Anthropic formalized the engineering practice
body:
“Context is a critical but finite resource for AI agents.”

Anthropic describes context engineering as the natural progression of prompt engineering: curating and maintaining the optimal tokens available during inference—including system instructions, tools, MCP, retrieved data, memory, and history.

Important distinction: the source describes an engineering discipline and design guidance, not a parallel 1,000-person training program.

Source: Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents, Sept. 29, 2025

title: Prompt engineering optimizes an instruction. Context engineering optimizes a system.
body:
PROMPT ENGINEERING
• Wording and structure of instructions
• Often one call or one task
• Primary question: What should we ask?

CONTEXT ENGINEERING
• System prompt, retrieval, tools, memory, history, and intermediate state
• Repeated decisions across an agent loop
• Primary question: What should the model see now—and what must it not see?

title: In healthcare, context is both a quality boundary and a privacy boundary
body:
The same context decision can determine whether an agent is useful, wrong, unsafe, or noncompliant.

Protected health information can enter through retrieval results, tool outputs, message history, or memory—then reach inference or persist in traces.

title: Trace the complete context lifecycle
body:
SOURCE → RETRIEVAL / TOOLS → CONTEXT GUARD → MODEL → MEMORY

At every boundary ask:
• What entered?
• Was it authorized, relevant, current, and minimal?
• What transformation occurred?
• What reached inference?
• What was persisted?

The earliest enforceable boundary is usually the best intervention point.

title: What participants will be able to do
body:
1. Read MLflow traces to find synthetic PHI in retrieval, tools, model context, and memory.

2. Diagnose poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash from span evidence.

3. Select fixes for chunking, retrieval timing, progressive disclosure, tool ambiguity, and memory policy.

4. Compare before/after traces to prove both privacy and quality improvements.

title: Read a trace like a context engineer
body:
1. ROOT AGENT — task, configuration, outcome
2. RETRIEVAL — scope, chunks, relevance, sensitive data
3. CONTEXT GUARD — drop, redact, transform, or pass through
4. TOOL ROUTING — available tools, selected tool, returned data
5. MODEL — exact context available at inference
6. MEMORY — what the run persisted

Do not start with the final answer. Find the first bad span.

title: Four context failure modes
body:
POISONING — untrusted context tries to alter agent behavior.

DISTRACTION — irrelevant volume crowds out the useful signal.

CONFUSION — stale, mixed, or contradictory evidence makes the answer uncertain.

CLASH — overlapping instructions or tool definitions compete.

Source for taxonomy: Drew Breunig, How Long Contexts Fail, June 2025

title: Combined lab
body: Diagnose one healthcare agent from broken trace to verified fix

title: The broken care-navigation agent
body:
USER TASK
“What follow-up care is needed after discharge for this patient?”

SEEDED FAILURES
• Patient name, MRN, and diagnosis leak from retrieval and a tool
• An oversized chunk mixes current and archived policy
• A retrieved note contains a prompt-injection instruction
• Two overlapping tools expose the wrong capability
• Raw conversation memory persists the sensitive answer

All patient-like values are fictional workshop markers.

title: Exercise 1: follow the synthetic PHI
body:
In the broken trace, locate:
• The first span containing an identifier or diagnosis
• The point where it crosses into model context
• The tool output that repeats it
• The memory span that persists it

Decision: where should the system intervene before inference and before persistence?

Real-system rule: traces themselves are a persistence surface. Avoid logging raw PHI.

title: Exercise 2: diagnose retrieval—not just the answer
body:
BROKEN
• Patient record included in a general policy task
• Giant chunk contains unrelated appendices
• Current 7-day guidance collides with archived 30-day guidance

FIX
• Filter to approved policy corpus and metadata
• Use smaller, policy-oriented chunks
• Preload stable safety rules
• Retrieve task-specific clinical policy just in time

title: Exercise 3: reduce tool clash with progressive disclosure
body:
BROKEN
Two tools share effectively identical descriptions:
• get_patient_summary
• search_clinical_policy

FIX
• Expose only the policy-search tool for a policy-only intent
• Give tools distinct purpose and data-boundary descriptions
• Require explicit, typed arguments
• Reveal patient-record capabilities only after intent and authorization checks

title: Prove the fix in the trace
body:
BEFORE → AFTER

Synthetic PHI locations: 4 → 0
Selected tool: patient summary → clinical policy
Retrieval: mixed patient + giant policy → small approved policy chunks
Model context: bloated and conflicting → concise and current
Memory: raw transcript → allowlisted de-identified summary

A better answer is encouraging. Better trace evidence is proof.

title: 45-minute workshop flow
body:
0–3 min — Setup and synthetic-data warning
3–10 min — Trace-reading primer
10–15 min — Generate the broken trace
15–25 min — Participant trace triage
25–32 min — Apply the remediation profile
32–39 min — Compare before/after traces
39–45 min — Debrief and exit check

Hands-on notebooks: fe-vm-hls-amer.cloud.databricks.com → /Shared/context-engineering-healthcare-agents

title: The durable operating principle
body:
Context is a product decision, a quality decision, and a security decision at the same time.

Trace the full lifecycle. Curate the minimum useful context. Intervene at the earliest enforceable boundary. Verify the change with evidence.
